subject: Private VPC networking follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@fintech.co>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned and to outline next steps: 

- Deployment mode: you indicated a strong preference for a Private VPC (customer-managed VPC / PrivateLink) to isolate traffic and meet data residency controls.
- Networking asks we captured: VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink (you preferred PrivateLink but open to peering for lower latency), IP allowlist for egress to Redwood control plane endpoints, and a static set of IPs for billing/ops.
- Security: SOC 2 and KMS integration required; you mentioned a pre-sales security questionnaire and standard procurement SOW.
- Performance targets: steady-state API latency under ~50ms p50 and burst QPS around 300 requests/min for the inference endpoint (rough numbers you gave).

Next steps I propose:
1) Please share a network contact who can join a 30–45 min call with our infra engineer (Sean) so we can walk through PrivateLink options and required allowlist ranges.
2) I’ve attached our internal network requirements doc (network diagram + recommended NAT/Egress patterns) and a short checklist for Private VPC onboarding.
3) If procurement needs a stub SOW or pricing, I can send a preliminary draft once we confirm the networking approach.

Attachments: internal_network_requirements.pdf (network diagram + checklist)

Happy to schedule the call — open windows: Tue/Wed mornings PST. Which works for you?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@fintech.co>

Thanks Marissa — great summary and appreciate the doc. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Deployment: we are leaning to PrivateLink over VPC peering due to tighter control over endpoints and ease for our security team.
- IP allowlist: we will need a set of stable egress IPs for our firewall team to allow; can you provide the ranges your control plane will use?
- KMS: we use AWS KMS (customer-managed) and will require instructions for key binding.
- Procurement: Procurement team (cc’d) will need a completed security questionnaire and a draft SOW. I’ve attached our standard security questionnaire; please fill and return.

I can make time Wed 06/23 at 10:00 AM PST for a technical sync — cc’ing the network engineer (procurement will coordinate SOW/PO).

Attachment: fintech_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf

Elena Rios
Head of Security & Infrastructure | FinTech Co
elena.rios@fintech.co

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@fintech.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up

Elena — thanks for the quick reply and the questionnaire. A few notes from our infra side (so the network folks have something concrete for the call):

- PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is fully supported and will expose a dedicated endpoint in your VPC. It avoids cross-account route table changes. VPC peering is possible but will require routing updates and careful egress handling.
- IP allowlist: for control plane interactions and metrics, our recommended egress ranges are 34.210.0.0/16 and 3.101.0.0/16 (please validate with your firewall team). If you require fixed single-IP NAT, we can discuss a transit NAT solution or use our Dedicated offering where egress IPs are static.
- Ports/protocols: outbound HTTPS (443) to the PrivateLink endpoint + port 22 only if you want SSH access for on-call debugging (optional).
- KMS: we support AWS KMS customer-managed keys; we’ll provide the IAM role and key policy template on the call.

I’ve pasted Marissa’s original message below for context. Can we lock Wed 2027-06-23 10:00 AM PST? If so I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: introductions, PrivateLink vs peering decision tree, IP allowlist/egress patterns, and next steps (SOW + timeline).

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com
